Definition: from G2450; "Judaism", i.e. the Jewish faith and usages:--Jews' religion.
BiblicalUsage: Judaism is the religion Paul left, and he names it when he tells his own story. In Galatians 1:13 he says, ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and in Galatians 1:14 he profited in the Jews' religion above many of his equals, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of his fathers.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Paul's past is the proof of grace: the most zealous defender of the old religion became its greatest preacher of the new one.
